name: Notify Me
summary: Shopify app to recover lost sales on out-of-stock products: back-in-stock notifications, pre-orders and wishlists that keep customers buying instead of bouncing.
best_for: Shopify stores that regularly sell out of popular products and want to recover that lost demand with back-in-stock notifications, pre-orders and wishlists
skip_if: you rarely run out of stock, or your store volume is too low for the recovered sales to outweigh the subscription
honest_knock: It does one job (turning out-of-stock moments into recovered sales via back-in-stock and pre-order alerts) and its value is entirely tied to how often you actually sell out. If your catalog rarely goes out of stock, you won't see much return. As with any Shopify app it's another monthly line item and another script on your storefront, so weigh it against the real revenue you're leaking to stock-outs.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-17 on the Shopify App Store listing at apps.shopify.com/preorder-back-in-stock, where the older address apps.shopify.com/back-in-stock-notifications now redirects, and in our own test on a development store the same day; earlier reads 2 and 23 September 2026) Four tiers on the listing: Lite free, Kickstart $9.90 a month or $79.21 a year, Starter $19.90 or $159.23 a year and Standard $39.90 or $319.26 a year, the yearly rates marked as a 33% saving. Until our 23 September reading the yearly rates were $95, $191 and $383 at a 20% saving, and the vendor's own page at notify-me.io/pricing still said “Save up to 20% on annual plans” on 17 November 2026; that page also listed an Enterprise tier arranged by meeting when we read it in September. Kickstart and Starter carry the same caps (500 alerts, 500 preorders); Standard raises them to 1,500 each, and the listing says unlimited plans are available inside the app. Preorders above the plan limit are $0.20 each and $0.15 on Standard; SMS and WhatsApp are priced per country. Kickstart is restricted to Basic Shopify stores in their first year, which the vendor's page repeated on 17 November 2026. Lite's allowances are mostly lifetime, not monthly: 100 back in stock requests, 5 preorders, 50 wishlist actions and 5 SMS and 5 WhatsApp messages over the life of the store, plus 10 notifications a month. 7 day trial and a 30 day money back guarantee. A temporary offer sat on top on 17 November 2026: each paid tier on the listing carried a “78% Off Until BFCM” label, and inside the app a banner read “Early bird: 78% off your first 2 months, until November 15”; in September the same tiers showed a discounted first month ($3.96, $7.96 and $15.96) instead. Inside the app on our development store the ladder was different again: Standard $39.90, Rocket $69.90 and Notify Me Plus $499.99 a month, or $319.26, $559.30 and $3,999.92 a year at 33% off, with development stores given free access to every plan, so check which ladder your own store is offered before you pick a tier.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested the Shopify app Notify Me! Back in Stock Alert on a development store: the install, the onboarding, the embed in an unsaved theme preview and one signup with a made up address. A Notify me button replaced Buy it now on the sold out product about 3 minutes after the start and opened a form for e-mail and SMS; the popup closed after the signup without a visible confirmation, the signup was not looked up in the dashboard and no alert was seen. The plan page of the development store showed only Standard, Rocket and Notify Me Plus, not the Lite, Kickstart and Starter plans of the dossier; choosing Standard (Yearly) gave no Shopify approval screen, so nothing was approved. The app was uninstalled afterwards. Install: the install form of the App Store listing (English) was submitted in our own tab at about 19:40 and the Shopify screen Install app asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data; the install was approved at about 19:41. In the App Store the app is called Notify Me! Back in Stock Alert - Premium Preorder, Wishlist, Waitlist (Restock), Low stock App (apps.shopify.com/preorder-back-in-stock); inside the Shopify admin it is called Notify! Back in stock|Preorder. The developer is Notify Me! in Richmond, BC, which fits notify-me.io in the dossier. The admin was in English. Onboarding: one box to accept the Terms of service of Notify Me! and Continue; then the screen Notify Me! has four features to boost your store with Back-in-Stock, Pre-order, Wishlist and Low-stock; Back-in-Stock, Pre-order and Wishlist were ticked and Low-stock was not, and the tester left only Back-in-Stock on; then App embed activation. No password and no sign-up form were shown. Core action, a Notify me button on a sold out product: the product was The Out of Stock Snowboard ($885.95, Sold out, already sold out, the stock was not changed). In the theme editor (the test-data theme, the Default product template, the App embeds tab) the embed Notify Me! was switched on and not saved. The preview showed Notify me in place of Buy it now at about 19:43, about 3 minutes after the start and about 8 actions after the install. A click on Notify me opened a popup Notify me via: with Email, SMS (NL (+31) and a Phone Number box) and the button Notify Me When Available. A made up test address was typed and the form was sent; the popup closed without any visible confirmation. No phone number was entered and no e-mail was sent or received. The signup was not looked up in the dashboard of the app and no back in stock alert was seen. The editor was left with Leave page (Leaving this page will delete all unsaved changes), so nothing was saved. Plans: after Activate later the app showed Development Store: Free Access to all plans, You are currently on a development store, selecting a plan will create a test charge at no cost, giving you full access to all premium features. Yearly (33% off): Standard $39.90 struck through, $26.61 a month, Billed annually at $319.26; Rocket (Most popular) $69.90, $46.61 a month, $559.3; Notify Me Plus $499.99, $333.33 a month, $3999.92. A banner said Early bird: 78% off your first 2 months, until November 15, and was still shown on 17 November. All three buttons said Start 7-day free trial. Limits in the app: Standard 1.500 notifications (pauses at limit), 1.500 PreOrders ($0.15 per extra PreOrder) and 10.000 Wishlist actions; Rocket 5.000 notifications, 10.000 PreOrders ($0.1 per extra) and 25.000 Wishlist actions; Notify Me Plus unlimited; $0.03 per SMS in US/CA on all three. Difference with the dossier and the listing: the dossier and the listing name Lite (free), Kickstart $9.90, Starter $19.90 and Standard $39.90 (the listing gives yearly prices of $79.21, $159.23 and $319.26 and the text 78% Off Until BFCM; the dossier gives yearly prices of $95, $191 and $383 and a Standard limit of 1.500 alerts, the app says 1.500 notifications), while the app on the development store showed only Standard $39.90, Rocket $69.90 and Notify Me Plus $499.99 and no Lite, Kickstart or Starter plan. Why the list differs, for example because of the development store, was not found out. The price fields are not changed here. Choosing a plan: Standard (Yearly) was chosen and the dialog Annual plan confirmation said Standard (Yearly), Billed annually $319.26/yr and that the 7-day free trial starts immediately and nothing is charged until the trial ends. Approve on Shopify was clicked, but no Shopify approval screen appeared and the page stayed on the plan page. So nothing was approved, no test charge was seen and the sentence that the test charge is not billed was not seen. Checkout: NOT reached, no Shopify approval screen, no card and no payment screen were seen. Cancelling: not tested, no plan was active. Not tested: a real notification or restock e-mail, SMS, pre-order, wishlist, low-stock, the list of signups in the dashboard, the Lite plan, an approved test charge and the cancel route. Clean up: no theme change was saved. The app was uninstalled through Settings, Apps with the reason Testing multiple apps; the screen said that Notify! Back in stock|Preorder was successfully uninstalled. Our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The popup closed after the signup without a visible confirmation; the dossier plans Lite, Kickstart and Starter were not shown on the development store; the Approve on Shopify button gave no approval screen; and an early bird banner still said until November 15 on 17 November.
